gaps.sentence: He did it ___ purpose, just to annoy her.
The tickets sold out ___ a matter of hours.
gaps.explanation: 'in a matter of hours' = within only a few hours.

gaps.sentence: Applications must be received ___ two weeks of the closing date.
gaps.explanation: 'Within two weeks' = not later than two weeks after.

gaps.sentence: ___ contrast to her sister, she loves publicity.
I did it ___ my own initiative — nobody asked me.
gaps.explanation: 'of one's own initiative' = without being asked.

gaps.sentence: The negotiations broke down ___ the very brink of success.
gaps.explanation: 'on the brink of' = on the point of.

gaps.sentence: Everything was packed ready in ___ of the movers' arrival.
The letter arrived ___ due course — three weeks later.
gaps.hint: ___ due course = at the expected time
gaps.explanation: 'in due course' = at the proper time eventually.
